newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine GDP up by around 4 pct in '96 - reports.
newsitem.headline: Argentine GDP up by around 4 pct in '96 - reports.

text.p: Argentina's economy grew by around four percent in 1996, Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said, according to Argentine newspapers Thursday.
"I believe that the GDP will grow by four percent in 1996, exceeding initial expectations," said Fernandez, quoted by the Clarin daily.
Fernandez, who is in Switzerland to attend the annual meeting of the World Economic Forum in Davos, was addressing a gathering of businesmen in Zurich.
Announcing a 10-year Eurobond in pesos, he said, "There will be no devaluation in Argentina in the next 10 years."
The government decided to launch the bond in pesos following requests from foreign investors, Fernndez said.
"The foreign investors were asking for it," he said. "The ones, for example, who invest in installations in pesos and must fund themselves in pesos as well."
Argentina's peso has been pegged at par with the U.S. dollar since 1991 and inflation has been cut to almost zero.

The government's earlier estimates for 1996 GDP growth were three to four percent, after a fall of 4.6 percent in 1995, when Argentina was lashed by the shockwaves of Mexico's December 1994 devaluation.
